summary: An April 1st joke RFC specifying how to send IPv4 and IPv6 packets using the Semaphore Flag Signaling System, with people waving flags. It is humorous and not meant for real deployment.

plainLanguage.summary: This April 1st joke describes sending IP packets with people waving flags. It gives the imagined system frame formats, acknowledgments, and retransmission rules.

questions: how does ip over semaphore flags work
what does an ip sfs frame contain
subtitle: An April 1st joke specifying how to transmit IP datagrams by waving semaphore flags.

tldr.problem: This April 1st RFC jokes about carrying IPv4 and IPv6 datagrams over semaphore flags.
tldr.mechanism: It encodes data as four-bit signals, adds frame and control signals, and describes a human-operated half-duplex link.
tldr.outcome: IP-SFS is a humorous, deliberately impractical transmission proposal, not a real deployment recommendation.

today: RFC 4824 is an Informational April 1st joke document describing IP over semaphore flags.

sections.title: IP over Semaphore Signaling
sections.content:
The memo defines IP-SFS as a method to send IPv4 and IPv6 packets over the Semaphore Flag Signaling System. It describes a half-duplex, point-to-point optical channel using two human-operated interfaces.

The protocol is placed at the link layer beneath IP. The memo limits the specification to unicast transmission and jokes about the physical demands on its operators.
sections.plainLanguage: The imagined link uses people waving flags to carry packets between two interfaces. It is described as one-way-at-a-time communication.

sections.title: Frames and Signals
sections.content:
IP-SFS maps 16 data signals to values 0 through 15, so each signal carries a four-bit nibble. A frame begins with FST and ends with FEN; it includes protocol and checksum fields, a frame number, data, and a CRC.

Control signals include ACK, NAK, RTR, and RTT. SUN can undo a signal and FUN can request a frame restart, with names that reinforce the April 1st humor.
sections.plainLanguage: Each flag pattern carries four bits. Other patterns mark frame boundaries, confirm receipt, or request another transmission.

sections.title: Transmission Limits and Security
sections.content:
The protocol describes Idle, Transmitting, and Receiving states, including retries when a frame fails its checksum. It allows up to 255 frames per session and up to 255 octets of payload per frame.

The memo says visibility and illumination affect error rates and that the protocol is insecure because it relies on line of sight. It discourages sending sensitive data unless higher-level protocols provide security.
sections.plainLanguage: Operators resend frames when errors occur, but visibility and human speed limit the link. The RFC warns that the signaling is insecure for sensitive data.
